title: Extract notification building from orders and subscriptions into a notifications feature
prompt:
Orders and subscriptions each keep their own private copy of the code that builds receipt and reminder messages: choosing email or SMS from the customer's preference, formatting dates and money, and the message wording. Extract that logic into a new feature, src/main/features/notifications, and make both features use it. Move the code, do not copy it: delete the old copies, and leave no re-export shim or wrapper behind. Orders and subscriptions keep only what is specific to them (the lines of an order receipt, the text of a renewal reminder, their totals).

notifications/index.ts exports exactly the following and nothing else.

Types: Recipient = { readonly name: string; readonly email: string; readonly phone?: string; readonly preferredChannel: 'email' | 'sms'; readonly utcOffsetMinutes: number } and Message, an email message { channel: 'email'; to: string; subject: string; body: string } or an sms message { channel: 'sms'; to: string; text: string } (all readonly, with the keys in this order). orderReceipt, orderReminder, subscriptionReceipt and subscriptionReminder keep their names and parameter order, take a Recipient where they take the customer or subscriber today, and return a Message. Neither feature may keep its own declaration of these shapes or of the 'email' | 'sms' union.

Functions:
- formatDate(at: Date, utcOffsetMinutes: number): string. The day, a three-letter English month and the year of the instant at the given offset, e.g. '5 Mar 2026'.
- formatMoney(cents: number): string. Cents is a non-negative integer; '$12.05', '$0.05'.
- chooseChannel(recipient: Recipient, now: Date): 'email' | 'sms'. 'sms' when the recipient prefers sms, has a phone that is not empty or only whitespace, and now is not in quiet hours (below); otherwise 'email'.
- receiptMessage(input: { readonly recipient: Recipient; readonly now: Date; readonly heading: string; readonly lines: readonly string[]; readonly totalCents: number }): Message. Email: subject 'Receipt: <heading>', body 'Hi <name>,\n\n<lines joined by \n>\n\nTotal: <money>\nIssued <date of now>\n'. SMS (to the phone as given): text '<heading>: total <money> (<date of now>)'.
- reminderMessage(input: { readonly recipient: Recipient; readonly now: Date; readonly heading: string; readonly text: string; readonly dueAt: Date }): Message. Email: subject 'Reminder: <heading>', body 'Hi <name>,\n\n<text>\n\nDue <date of dueAt>\nSent <date of now>\n'. SMS: text '<heading>: <text> (due <date of dueAt>)'.
Every date is formatted at the recipient's utcOffsetMinutes. The channel of both builders is chosen by chooseChannel.

Behavior: every message the four feature functions produce today must stay byte for byte the same, and test/orders.test.ts, test/subscriptions.test.ts and test/composition-root.test.ts must keep passing without any edit. The two copies disagree in two places, and in both the result below wins for orders and subscriptions alike: (1) orders formats its dates in UTC while subscriptions uses the recipient's offset; use the recipient's offset everywhere, so an order receipt or reminder now prints each date in the customer's utcOffsetMinutes. (2) For a recipient who prefers sms but has an empty or whitespace-only phone, orders falls back to email while subscriptions texts the empty number; fall back to email. Nothing else about either feature's output changes.

One new rule, which the extraction makes a single change: quiet hours. SMS is never sent from 22:00 (inclusive) to 07:00 (exclusive) local time, where local time is now shifted by the recipient's utcOffsetMinutes (offsets are whole minutes and may be negative or not a whole hour, e.g. 330). In that window chooseChannel returns 'email' and the builders produce the email message, exactly as if the recipient had no phone. Because the features build their messages through notifications, orders and subscriptions follow the rule without further change; the composition root must not choose a channel itself.

Add tests for the notifications API, including both disagreements and the quiet-hours boundaries, in test/notifications.test.ts. Run nitpicker-gate until it exits 0.
